original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Classify pairs of 2-dimensional F2 column planes of minimum weight at least 2 whose image spaces meet only at 0, up to coordinate permutation, and count the orbits.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register alphabet. This package stays in the abelian F2 rank-one idempotent model and answers open question 1 of #7221: which pairs of minimum-weight-at-least-2 column planes have trivial image intersection, and how many coordinate-permutation orbits those pairs form. No new alphabet, word, or kappa is claimed. The same card was already moved to scalar pattern-pool questions by #5921, #6838, #6921, #6962, #7094, #7138, #7139, and #7221.
bottleneck_link: Side result. The orbit classification does not price a word, so the original native acceptance gate remains unmet. The selected frontier is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop once the weight-(2,2,2) pairs are classified by an exhaustive case split and the unrestricted minimum-weight-at-least-2 orbit set is proved infinite by an explicit family. Do not classify the normal-normal or mixed geometries.
evidence: PROOF.md classifies one column plane by integer triples, splits every weight-(2,2,2) pair into five orbits, and gives an explicit infinite family of inequivalent pairs. verify.py exhausts the finite weight-(2,2,2) domain on widths 5 through 9, locks the labeled counts 0, 900, 2100, 1120, 0, separates the five orbits by support size, cross count, and overlap, and checks the doubling family together with the pool-W witness.

open_questions.question: Which minimum-weight-at-least-2 column-column orbits remain after every coordinate that is a duplicate of another coordinate, in both planes, has been deleted in pairs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The doubling family lies over the printed weight-(2,2,2) orbit. Pool W shows that a weight-(2,2,4) plane need not have such a core. A reduction theorem would separate padding from new plane types.
open_questions.first_step: For a plane whose three type-multiplicities are all even or all positive, delete two coordinates of one repeated type and test whether both planes stay 2-dimensional and of minimum weight at least 2.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package proves infinitude and the weight-(2,2,2) census. It does not run that deletion on every orbit.

open_questions.question: Is every dimension-6 pool built from two normal-form triples, or from one normal-form triple and one column triple, a coordinate permutation of the corresponding witness printed in #7139?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those are the other two geometries in #7139 Section 7. The column-column orbits classified here do not decide them.
open_questions.first_step: Use the normal-form uniqueness statement on one 3-set in #7139 Section 2, then check whether two disjoint blocks can be moved simultaneously onto the printed coordinates.
open_questions.blocked_by: The general case split that sorts every dimension-6 pool into one of the three geometries is #7139's argument and is not reproved here.
